title: Don't Talk About It. Be It!
html:
We say we want to be at something. Better husbands. Better dads. Better men. Better anything.

We talk about it. We announce it. We say, "Look at me. I'm doing my best here."

But trying isn't becoming.

But here's the truth:

  1. You don't have to talk about it.
  2. You don't have to journal it.
  3. You just have to be

I want to be the rock for my family. So I'm being the rock. Just like I said, I would be. Just like my wife has written in cards to me.

Not perfectly. Not overtly. Just consistently.

When I catch myself off-track, I ask,

"What would a well-rounded man do right now?"

Not what Ifeel like doing — but what the well-rounded man I'm becoming would choose.

At a certain age, we already know what to do. That wisdom is built in. It's instinct.

But we bury it under the stories we tell ourselves. Stories born from pain, excuses, or past failures.

Strip away the story. What's left?

Clarity.

Action.

Peace.

I want to be a safe space for my wife — so Iam a safe space.

It was hard at first. But, like most good things, it's getting easier with practice.

And it feels great! Like this is how it's meant to be.

So today, whatever's in front of you…

Don't overthink it. Don't avoid it. Just be the thing.
